:::{#thm-hadamard-distance}
#### Minimum distance of the Hadamard code

The [Hadamard code](#def-hadamard-code) is a [linear code](#def-linear-code)
with [minimum distance](#def-hamming-distance) $2^{k-1}$.

:::

::: {.proof}
Let $x \ne 0$, and pick $i$ with $x_i = 1$.
Let $e_i$ have a 1 in position $i$ only.
Then $\langle x, a + e_i \rangle = \langle x, a \rangle + 1$,
so pairing each $a$ with $a + e_i$ pairs a 0 with a 1,
and exactly half of the $2^k$ entries of the codeword of $x$ are 1.
So every nonzero message has a codeword of [weight](#def-weight) $2^{k-1} \ge 1$.
Each inner product $\langle x, a \rangle$ is linear in $x$,
so the encoding map is linear,
and only the zero message has the zero codeword,
so the map is one-to-one and the code is linear.
Then @rem-linear-code-weight gives the minimum distance.

:::
